verdict.justification: Both deliverables accurately identify the 48 POs that shipped in June ($145,218.80 order value, $140,008.20 shipped value, $5,210.60 short-shipped) and the 5 POs with a full June ship window that slipped to July ($13,300.00 order value, $13,248.00 shipped value). However, Deliverable B is better constructed for the explicit requirement that the summary tables be filterable by account name. In Deliverable B's summary tables on Sheet 1, the total rows use `SUBTOTAL(109,...)` so that when an account manager filters the summary table by account, the totals dynamically recalculate for visible rows. Deliverable A uses static `SUM(...)` formulas in its Sheet 1 summary tables (`formula=SUM(B20:B26)` and `formula=SUM(B32:B38)`), which do not update when rows are filtered, and it clutters Table 2 with zero-value rows for accounts that had no slipped POs. Deliverable B also provides more actionable commentary (breaking down the largest short-shipped accounts and the account-level breakdown of the July slippage right in the summary text) and organizes its supporting exceptions cleanly on a dedicated fourth tab.

decisive_issues.issue: Summary tables on Sheet 1 use SUM instead of SUBTOTAL, so totals do not dynamically update when filtered by account.
Table 2 includes zero-value rows for accounts with no slipped orders (Dolce, Five O Fore, Hunt's) and uses static SUM.
